the_day: Google launched a Gemini agent for business work, Anthropic changed its usage policy and committed $150 million to a federal science program, the Financial Times put OpenAI's annualized revenue $20 billion below earlier signals, and USA Today sued OpenAI.

items.headline: Anthropic updates usage policy to ban abusive behavior toward Claude
points: Anthropic published a 2026 Usage Policy update adding rules on model abuse, deception and election interference.
The Verge reports the policy now bans "abusive or cruel behavior" toward Claude.
Firstpost reports users who abuse Claude could lose access to it.
items.for_you: Claude users who break the new rules, including abusive conduct toward the model, risk losing access.

items.headline: Anthropic commits $150 million to the federal Genesis Mission
points: Anthropic announced a $150 million commitment over three years to the Genesis Mission, a federal AI science initiative.
Unite.AI reports it covers three years of Claude support for the Department of Energy program.
Benzinga describes the Genesis Mission as White House-backed.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO documents reportedly show over $40 billion in losses
points: Unconfirmed: Mashable reports Anthropic's IPO documents show more than $40 billion in losses last year.
Yahoo Finance separately reports Anthropic plans to spend $518 billion on cloud and computing power.

sources.title: Anthropic IPO docs reportedly reveal over $40 billion in losses last year

items.headline: CrowdStrike says suspected Chinese hacker used Claude against South Korean banks
points: CrowdStrike says a suspected Chinese hacker used Claude and an AI agent to steal data from South Korean banks.
The Register reports the evidence came from exposed AI logs that included a possible hacker's CV.
China called the claim false information for political purposes, and the accused 26-year-old says he is being framed, Wccftech reports.

items.headline: Anthropic also halved Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices
points: SiliconANGLE reports Anthropic halved cache-read prices for Sonnet 5.5 alongside the Haiku 5.5 release.
OpenTools notes that migrating between models can still change your bill.
dev.ua reports Haiku 5.5 costs more for long queries despite its lower base price.
items.for_you: Developers who use prompt caching with Sonnet 5.5 should see lower cache-read costs.

items.headline: Google Cloud launches a Gemini agent for long-running work tasks
points: Google Cloud introduced a "universal" Gemini agent that carries out tasks across business apps, Reuters and Bloomberg report.
VentureBeat reports the agents can run for days and get their own Gmail, Calendar and Drive storage.
TechCrunch says it starts with businesses; India Today reports it can work on behalf of groups of people.
items.for_you: Businesses using Google's work apps can hand Gemini longer, multi-step tasks instead of single prompts.

items.headline: Meta, Walmart and Stripe back an open standard for AI shopping agents
points: The Daily Caller reports big tech and retail companies are teaming up on an open standard for AI shopping agents.
Yahoo Tech first reported yesterday that Meta, Walmart and Stripe launched the standard; this is a second report.

sources.title: Big Tech And Retail Giants Team Up To Tame AI Shopping Bots

items.headline: OpenAI annualized revenue is $50 billion, $20 billion below earlier signals
points: The Financial Times reports OpenAI's annualized revenue is about $50 billion, roughly $20 billion less than previously signaled.
Quartz reports OpenAI corrected its annualized revenue figure to $50 billion.
CNBC reports shares of Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave and other AI companies fell after the report.

items.headline: USA Today sues OpenAI for copyright infringement
points: USA Today filed a copyright infringement lawsuit against OpenAI over AI training, Reuters reports.
Forbes says the suit claims OpenAI unlawfully used its reporting to train and operate its models.
Bloomberg Law reports other news outlets are joining the copyright fight against OpenAI.

items.headline: OpenAI disrupts influence operations that used fake journalists and think tanks
points: OpenAI says it disrupted two AI-enabled influence operations that used false-front journalists and a think tank to spread geopolitical messaging.
CyberScoop reports OpenAI tied the operations to Iran and Russia.
NBC News reports that, according to OpenAI, the Russian operation tricked schools, a politician and media outlets.

items.headline: Senior OpenAI safety staffer resigns over safety concerns
points: A top OpenAI safety staffer has resigned and explained why in an interview on CNN's Amanpour.
TIKR quotes the departing staffer saying: "This is nuts…This is not right."

sources.title: A top OpenAI safety staffer just resigned. He tells Amanpour why.

items.headline: OpenAI's Decisions API reduces evaluations to yes, no or pick one
points: OpenAI has launched a Decisions API that reduces complex evaluations to a yes, no or pick-one answer, first reported yesterday by The Decoder.
Artificial Lawyer, the second outlet to report it, describes it as a cheaper way for lawyers to run bulk review.
items.for_you: Developers on the OpenAI API have a new option for high-volume yes-or-no evaluations.

sources.title: OpenAI Decisions - Cheaper Bulk Review For Lawyers

items.headline: Grok Bot can now search and monitor X directly
points: Crypto Briefing reports Grok Bot now has native X search and can analyze more than 100 posts per prompt.
Howl.link reports the feature also supports real-time monitoring and tracking on X.
items.for_you: Grok Bot users can pull live X posts into their tasks without a separate tool.

points: Elon Musk said SpaceXAI will be renamed SpaceXSI, BW Businessworld reports.
The move follows a Trump administration push to replace the term AI with "super intelligence"; Musk said "Yes, we will make that change."
